question: Should the publication queue retain a compacted per-target high-water fence indefinitely after detailed terminal entries expire?
rationale: That retention rule is a durable behavioral contract: it prevents reposts but can also suppress historical revisions after detailed audit metadata has been removed, so tests alone cannot choose the intended operational policy.

options.title: Accept the compacted fence with upgrade proof
options.body: Keep the design after showing that existing storage upgrades safely and that only stale revisions, never later valid revisions, are suppressed.

options.title: Retain detailed terminal rows instead
options.body: Avoid a long-lived high-water suppression rule at the cost of retaining more terminal publication metadata.

recommendation.title: Accept the compacted fence with upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Keep the design after showing that existing storage upgrades safely and that only stale revisions, never later valid revisions, are suppressed.

likelyOwner.reason: The available related-item history places this contributor closest to prior publication/state durability work, though ownership evidence is limited.
